clue.text: Much grandfatherly love, Ruby, from Fred Xx

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes those letters from it, leaving the remainder

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
red is the colour of ruby; taking it from Fred leaves one letter
the capital X is the Roman numeral for ten, and the small x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: A grandfather signs off a card to granddaughter Ruby with lots of love and kisses.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of Xx do different jobs: the capital is ten in Roman numerals, the small one the times sign. Ruby is not a name but its colour, red, which comes out of Fred.
explanation.definitionFit: Oftentimes is an old-fashioned word for 'often', so it is how a grandfather might say 'much' as in 'frequently'.

clue.text: Gold in reserve rarely in spherical form

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
by means aside or in reserve, as in 'put by'

explanation.surface: Gold held back in a reserve is seldom shaped like a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' belongs with the definition, warning that orby is an uncommon word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orby is a rare adjective meaning shaped like an orb, that is round or spherical.

clue.text: Aussie can bar northern youngster

indicators.note: bar as a verb means exclude or shut out, so a letter is kept out of the word

blocks.note: a tinny is Australian slang for a can of beer
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: An Australian beer can is kept from a young northerner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb and 'bar' like a pub, but the can is a noun and bar means exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is used as a noun for a small child, a youngster.

clue.text: Drafted in by musical group, axeman is still in the dark

indicators.note: someone drafted in is brought into a group, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians
a hewer is one who chops with an axe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guitarist drafted into a band still has no idea what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: An axeman is slang for a guitarist, which suits the band picture, but here he chops wood.
explanation.definitionFit: None the wiser means no better informed than before, so still ignorant of the facts.

clue.text: Wretched individual now a cult figure?

blocks.note: in means fashionable, of the now
a sect is a cult; the question mark flags the loose reading

explanation.surface: Is a miserable person the latest cult hero?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'cult figure' is not a celebrity: read the answer as two words, the first meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect is used figuratively of a contemptible or insignificant person, a wretch.

clue.text: Outside of Brian, this Python could be incredible

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters
could be means might become, in a different arrangement of the same letters

blocks.note: the word whose letters the answer plus two more could form
the first and last letters of Brian

explanation.surface: A fan's view: apart from the Life of Brian, this Python member's work could be incredible.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer with B and N outside it rearranges into incredible, so take those out of incredible and rearrange. Eric Idle was in Monty Python, which made the film Life of Brian.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty Python comedy team, so he is a Python.

clue.text: Castles on king's side, capturing pawns, mate

indicators.note: a piece that captures others takes them in, so one group of letters holds the other

blocks.note: O-O is the chess notation for castling on the king's side
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A chess move: castling kingside while taking pawns, then checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like checkmate, finishing the chess picture; it is the definition, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a colleague or friend, a counterpart, just as 'mate' means a pal.

clue.text: Busy loo in which a supporter joins end of queue

indicators.note: in which says the following words go inside the one before
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'queue'

blocks.note: a privy is an outdoor lavatory
taken as written
a golf tee supports the ball
the last letter of queue

explanation.surface: A crowded toilet where someone holds up the last person in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' looks like an adjective for the loo but is the noun: busy is old British slang for a police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is a detective, and a busy is British slang for a detective or police officer.

clue.text: Bored Elgar is maybe making an effort

blocks.note: to be off something is to have gone off it, tired of it
Elgar is the setter of this puzzle, so what he is doing is setting

explanation.surface: The puzzle's own setter, fed up, is still trying hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar names the setter of this very puzzle, not the composer. The definition is loose: offsetting is working to counterbalance something.
explanation.definitionFit: Offsetting means compensating or counterbalancing, which the setter stretches to mean making an effort to balance things out.

clue.text: Bachelor grandpa and the like a potential source of upset

blocks.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
grandpa and his kind are nana's kin, grandma's family

explanation.surface: An unmarried man, his grandfather and their sort are behind some family upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'grandpa and the like' as NANA'S KIN: grandpa and his relatives are kin of nana (grandma).
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is a slapstick cause of a fall, and figuratively any blunder that may trip someone up.

clue.text: Domestic servant at last provided folio

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the final letter of servant
provided that means if
F is the abbreviation for folio

explanation.surface: A household servant finally supplies a folio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' seems to go with servant, but it is a noun: a domestic is a household row.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is informal British for a quarrel between partners at home, and a tiff is a minor quarrel.

clue.text: Requirement of jilted bride at altar what crowded church affords?

blocks.note: what is required is a substitute, a stand-in
a bride left at the altar is missing the bridegroom

explanation.surface: A deserted bride and a packed church at the same wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as STAND-IN GROOM, the replacement a jilted bride needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing room is space to stand when the seats are full, which a packed church has to offer.

clue.text: All lines might be hosiery were grand to be invested

indicators.note: the answer becomes the other phrase only if a letter were put inside it, so that letter is absent from the answer

blocks.note: hosiery is the stocking trade, the business of selling stockings
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A shop's whole range would be hosiery if a thousand pounds were invested.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: put G inside the answer and you have a phrase meaning hosiery, so the answer is that phrase minus G.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-in-trade is the full range of goods a shop keeps, which in retail are its lines.

clue.text: Hand-measuring device a complete disaster, finally scrapped

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
something scrapped is broken up, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of disaster

explanation.surface: A device for measuring hands proves a total flop and is ditched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disaster' looks like the anagram signal for 'a complete', but only its last letter is used; 'scrapped' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapometer gauges the loudness of applause on TV talent shows, measuring hands clapping.

clue.text: Palace so short, not entirely short of canvas

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the final letter is cut
not entirely means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
a ship short of canvas has no sails

explanation.surface: The palace is so small it cannot quite fill a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests a painting but means sailcloth, so short of canvas is without sails. Each piece then loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the royal palace built by Louis XIV outside Paris.

clue.text: Songs by Mendelssohn one conducts in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience hears, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: one who conducts is a leader

explanation.surface: A concert of Mendelssohn's songs, with a conductor heard in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, and Mendelssohn wrote many, as well as his Songs without Words.

clue.text: Ringing the chap with the map?

blocks.note: a plan is a map or diagram
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: Calling the man who holds the map on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' puts the chap alongside the map, and the map comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant, often mournful sound, such as that of ringing bells.

clue.text: Fancy lovely securing mariner's heart after Bluto's exit?

definitions.text: Fancy lovely securing mariner's heart after Bluto's exit?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece goes inside
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or made-up, so these letters are rearranged
the exit of a word is where it ends, its last letter
after places the rearranged piece behind the letter before it

blocks.note: the last letter of Bluto
the word to be rearranged
the central letter of mariner

explanation.surface: Popeye the sailor's lovely sweetheart, wanted once his rival Bluto has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: in the Popeye cartoons, Olive Oyl is the mariner's fancy, the woman his rival Bluto is always after.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive Oyl is Popeye's girlfriend, the object of both the sailor's and Bluto's affection in the cartoons.

clue.text: Slip by so easily, perhaps

indicators.note: something done easily is loose and free, so these letters move around freely

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone may get past without much trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Possibly and perhaps are synonyms, both expressing that something may be so.

clue.text: My work was on war and the point of writing about that in verse

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a nib is the point of a pen
yon is a poetic word for that

explanation.surface: A war poet introduces himself and his craft.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Binyon wrote 'For the Fallen', the First World War poem read on Remembrance Day ('They shall grow not old').
explanation.definitionFit: Binyon is best known for poetry about the First World War, so he could say his work was on war.

clue.text: Parson visiting Big Apple with rampant dragon

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so one piece sits within the other
rampant means rearing up, and in a down entry rising up reads the letters backwards

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the Big Apple is New York, NY
Rev is short for Reverend, a parson's title

explanation.surface: A vicar on a trip to New York with a fierce dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' is the heraldic term for a beast rearing up, apt for a dragon, but here it turns the visit upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a heraldic dragon with two legs and wings.

clue.text: Enchanting chap takes auxiliary diplomat on first trip

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one word surrounds the others

blocks.note: a mage is a magician, a man who casts spells
an aid is something auxiliary, a help
an envoy is a diplomat

explanation.surface: A charming man brings an assistant diplomat on his first journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enchanting' looks like charming, but means casting spells, which is a mage's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage is a ship's first ever trip, maiden meaning first or untried.

clue.text: A small way to promote energy and verve

indicators.note: promoting something moves it up the line, so a letter is taken from the end and set at the front

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
a lane is a small road

explanation.surface: A small route to boosting one's energy and liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, promoting a letter lifts it to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan and verve are synonyms for vigour, flair and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Repost egotist's favourite online image

blocks.note: an egotist's favourite person is me
posting it again repeats the same two letters

explanation.surface: Sharing again the egotist's top picture online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repost' says post the same thing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a humorous image or video passed around and copied on the internet.

clue.text: Something for carrying money up to work

blocks.note: first meaning: a cash register or money drawer
second meaning: until
third meaning: to cultivate soil, as a farmer does

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: a money drawer, a preposition for time, and a verb for farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Till is a cash drawer in a shop, a word for until, and a verb meaning to plough or work the land.

clue.text: Another helping of dessert here? I'd be unwise …

blocks.note: more is another helping of food
a fool is a dessert of fruit purée and cream
here, from the speaker's view, is me

explanation.surface: A diner asks for seconds of pudding, then thinks better of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' as the speaker refers to themself is a common crossword convention for ME. A fool is a British pudding, such as gooseberry fool.
explanation.definitionFit: 'More fool me' is an idiom admitting one's own foolishness, as in 'I would be unwise to do that'.

clue.text: … here's trolley, there's trifle (or tart) and beware staff carrying others …

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within, so the letters sit inside the words in front

blocks.note: surface padding, though the same four letters also lurk across each of these pairs of words
the letters span the end of beware and the start of staff

explanation.surface: A dessert trolley on show, with a warning to staff wheeling other treats.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters also sit across 'here's trolley' and 'there's trifle'; 'carrying' points to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest means the others, the remaining ones of a group.

clue.text: … that one adult's leaving to eat 80 per cent of fruit dessert

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed from the word
eighty per cent of a five-letter word keeps its first four letters
eating takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the previous answer, rest, means the balance, the remainder
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
the first four of five letters of mango

explanation.surface: Continuing the trolley scene: a grown-up leaves after eating most of a fruit pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That one' points back to the rest in the clue before, here read as the balance. Take out one A and put most of mango inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Blancmange is a sweet set milk pudding, a classic British dessert.
